system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: HOPE-3 NCT00468923 - Heart Outcomes Prevention Evaluation-3
Investigational drug: rosuvastatin
Document: Rosuvastatin in hemodialysis: short-term effects on lipids and C-reactive protein (journal, published 2009-01-01, source pmid:19229822)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Rosuvastatin in hemodialysis: short-term effects on lipids and C-reactive protein

BACKGROUND: Patients on regular hemodialysis present high cardiovascular mortality. Uremic dyslipidemia and inflammation take part in the etiology of atherosclerosis. Rosuvastatin calcium has not been studied in patients on dialysis to date. We sought to evaluate the results of rosuvastatin therapy regarding lipids, lipoproteins and a marker of inflammation in hemodialysis patients. METHODS: In a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial, 59 patients on hemodialysis (31 in the placebo group, and 28 taking rosuvastatin 10 mg/day) were followed for 3 months. Lipids, lipoproteins and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) were measured at baseline, 30 days and 3 months. RESULTS: In the rosuvastatin group, there was a significant decrease from baseline to the study end in total cholesterol (163+/-53 mg/dL to 142+/-43 mg/dL; p<0.05), in LDL cholesterol (90+/-39 mg/dL to 69+/-32 mg/dL; p<0.05) and in non-HDL cholesterol (121+/-46 mg/dL to 99+/-39 mg/dL; p<0.05). In the placebo group, no significant decrease was observed. High-sensitivity CRP was lower in the rosuvastatin than in the placebo group at 3 months (p<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin calcium at 10 mg/day was effective in lowering total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol and hs-CRP in hemodialysis patients.
--- END ---

Extract the facts.
